summary: Freeze the combined #71/#83 durable persistence contract before production changes: corrupt or unsupported committed durable state must fail closed before user code can overwrite it; POSIX files must remain private under umask(0); and a pre-planted predictable temp symlink must never redirect checkpoint bytes outside durableRoot.
steps: Re-read current M10 publishDurable/readDurable/dropDurable on the protocol-v5 main after #81/#82 merged.

Froze the repair direction: replace the payload+metadata pair with one self-describing committed generation and a single atomic rename commit point; use exclusive private temp files and fail closed on invalid existing committed state.

Added public-behavior RED regressions for corruption/version mismatch preventing user code, POSIX permissions under a permissive umask, and the legacy predictable temp-symlink attack without depending on the future committed filename layout.

evidence.note: Confirmed payload is renamed before metadata is separately written, no fsync is used, readDurable catches all validation errors as absence, file modes inherit umask, and the temp filename is predictable (`target + .tmp- + pid`) with writeFileSync following a planted symlink.
Production code is intentionally unchanged; GitHub Actions will capture the baseline failures before the storage-format patch.

limitations: The documented 64 MiB aggregate durable quota is tracked by #89 and will be implemented immediately after the crash-consistent format exists.
Windows ACL hardening is not represented by POSIX mode-bit assertions; Windows remains covered by ownership expectations and full runtime regression.
